Three things the run established about the loop itself, all recorded in .claude/artifacts/loop-log.json:

1. The threshold argument is unreachable on helios by construction. addressable keeps ss-aio's 525 GL-blocked regions in the denominator while they cannot be covered, capping the submodule near 48%.
2. Stage 5's addressable formula divides a line count by a region denominator. The real figure came from re-running the classifier.
3. The marginal-gain floor STILL has never executed -- the queue emptied in one iteration, so the stop rule this issue most wanted to exercise remains untested. A second run, on hyperspace, would be the way to reach it.

Fixed: the guard now tracks cd across the command line, so a git call is resolved against the directory it will actually run in rather than the payload's session cwd.

cd hills && git commit, with hills on master, now refuses and names hills. Before the fix it allowed, reporting 'commit in screen-savers on <branch>' -- the superproject's branch, for a commit landing in the submodule.

A cd is applied whatever separator precedes it, and only if the target exists: a cd that would fail leaves the shell where it was under ';' and short-circuits the rest under '&&', so either way not applying it is right.

Two defects, not one. 'frame = 0;' in the constructor closed the first-frame collision -- reproduced with placement-new over 0xFF storage as vertices=0, indices=1752. Independent review then found the fix was half a fix: frame is an unsigned short and init() zeroes every cubedata *_frame, so the counter collides again every time it wraps, roughly every 18 minutes at 60fps. advanceFrame() re-zeroes the per-cube counters on the wrap and restarts at 1.

The wrap is the more serious of the two. Reproduced by landing the wrap on a frame where the surface reaches fresh cubes: 294 vertices expected, 0 emitted -- the crawl seed reads as already-done and the object disappears for that frame.

A static field hides it completely, which is why the first attempt at a wrap test ran 70000 frames with the bug present and reported nothing. Recorded as L6-F4: a test can be genuinely discriminating for the defect it was written for and structurally blind to a second defect in the same three lines.

Also from the review of this work, all fixed: unchecked index dereferences in the new suite; getIndex reverted from indices.data()[i], which was a change that made it worse; and three comments corrected, including the false premise that the *_vertex_index fields were never written (cubedata is an aggregate, so resize() value-initialises them).

A sweep for the same bug class across impCubeVolume's other members came back clean -- currentVertexIndex and currentCubeIndex are assigned in neither constructor nor init() but are reset at the top of every overload that reads them. The design field records why frame was different: it is a generation counter that must persist, so there was no natural reset point.
